title: Why lost people walk in circles (opening test)

lines.text: This hiker is walking in a perfectly straight line. At least, that's what he thinks.
He's lost in a German forest, so he picks a direction and commits. No turning. No stopping.
An hour later, he finds a campfire. Someone's been here! Help is close!
He marches on, dead straight. Another hour. Another campfire. Same log. Same sad sausage.
It's his campfire. He's been walking in circles.
And scientists say you would too.

experiment.hypothesis: Ricks Clips structure: a comic escalating story with the science reveal later, a cut every ~2 s across several small sets, face close-ups, near-continuous narration.
facts: Souman, Frissen, Sreenivasa & Ernst, 'Walking straight into circles', Current Biology 19:1538 (2009): GPS-tracked walkers in the Bienwald forest (Germany) and the Sahara walked in circles when the sun was hidden, repeatedly crossing their own path without noticing; with the sun or moon visible they kept fairly straight; blindfolded walkers made circles as small as 20 m across. https://www.mpg.de/596269/pressrelease200908171
